title: Eight years of wanting, three months of building with AI
description: Lalit Maganti built syntaqlite (high-fidelity devtools for SQLite) after procrastinating for 8 years. Used Claude Code to overcome initial hurdle with 400+ grammar rules. Key insight: AI made procrastination on design decisions worse because refactoring felt cheap. First AI prototype worked as proof of concept but lacked coherent architecture. Second attempt with more human-in-the-loop design took longer but produced robust library. AI weakness: struggles when you don't know what you want and when tasks have no objectively checkable answer (design vs implementation).
author: Simon Willison (linking to Lalit Maganti)

title: scan-for-secrets 0.2: CLI tool for scanning secrets before sharing
description: Released a Python CLI tool that scans files for secrets before publishing. Built using README-driven-development with Claude Code. Features include streaming results, multiple directory scanning, individual file scanning, Python API functions, and verbose mode. Scans for common encodings (backslash, JSON escaping) of secrets, not just literal matches.
author: Simon Willison

title: Syntaqlite Playground: SQLite validation in the browser
description: Built a web-based playground for syntaqlite (SQLite parser, formatter, and validator). Compiled the C/Rust library to WebAssembly to run in Pyodide in browser. Provides UI for formatting, parsing into AST, validating, and tokenizing SQLite SQL queries with schema definitions.
author: Simon Willison

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Discussion questioning whether AI coding provides actual speedup over manual coding, exploring the debate about the 'last 10%' of coding quality and whether AI tools truly enhance productivity.
author: Hacker News community

title: GitHub platform activity surging
description: GitHub had 1 billion commits in 2025, now 275 million per week on pace for 14 billion in 2026 if linear. GitHub Actions grew from 500M minutes/week in 2023 to 1B in 2025, now 2.1B minutes per week.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Kyle Daigle, GitHub COO)

title: LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Discussion about using multi-step AI pipelines with LLMs, including 3D mesh generation with validation stages. Mentions challenges with LLMs skipping edge cases and the practical realities of AI-assisted development workflows.
author: Hacker News community

title: Vulnerability Research Is Cooked
description: Thomas Ptacek analyzes how frontier models are transforming vulnerability research. Within months, coding agents will drastically alter exploit development economics. LLMs excel at this due to baked-in knowledge of bug classes (stale pointers, integer mishandling, type confusion), pattern matching abilities across vast codebases, and the ability to run unlimited test trials. Kernel security reports have jumped from 2-3 per week to 5-10 per day, with duplicate reports becoming common.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Thomas Ptacek)

title: Linux kernel security reports surge due to AI
description: Linux kernel security reports jumped from 2-3 per week to 5-10 per day since beginning of 2026. Most reports are now correct, requiring more maintainers. Previously saw 'AI slop' but world switched - now receiving real, good reports made with AI. Seeing daily duplicate reports where same bug found by different people using different tools.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Willy Tarreau, Daniel Stenberg, Greg Kroah-Hartman)

title: How I write software with LLMs
description: Practical guide using a hierarchy of AI agents with different personas (architect, business analyst, security expert) for comprehensive AI-assisted development workflows.
author: Hacker News community

title: Gemma 4: Byte for byte, the most capable open models
description: Google released four new vision-capable Apache 2.0 licensed reasoning LLMs sized at 2B, 4B, 31B, plus a 26B-A4B Mixture-of-Experts. The models emphasize unprecedented intelligence-per-parameter efficiency, with smaller models using Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE) for on-device deployments. All models natively process video and images, with E2B and E4B models featuring native audio input for speech recognition.
author: Simon Willison

title: I'm a junior developer, and to be honest, in 2026 AI is...
description: A developer's perspective on using AI tools to generate code, fix bugs, and refactor logic. Discusses AI writing 'cleaner' code and the impact on development workflows from a junior developer's experience.
author: Reddit user - r/ArtificialInteligence
